A Welcome From
Our Headteacher
I would like to personally welcome you to Sunny Bank Primary School.
Sunny Bank is a proud part of The Island Learning Trust, alongside Halfway Houses and Minster-in-Sheppey, sharing a passion to create a positive and rewarding journey, setting high standards.
The school has been transformed since becoming part of the Island Learning Trust (TILT).
With a relentless focus on improving children’s outcomes, so that they can be successful in their future lives, they now have high aspirations and expectations for themselves and their families.
The staff at Sunny Bank are passionate about building a school based on the foundations of success, where our pupils feel safe, happy and secure and can learn and develop skills that enable them to become lifelong learners. This is underpinned by our school vision, values and our Sunny Bank pupil’s character below.
Every staff member, parent and leader strives hard to be the best that we can be to ensure that our children can be the best that they can be.

Reception Intake

French
French
At Sunny Bank we aim to teach children another language to provide them with a broader understanding of the world around them. Being exposed to a Modern Foreign Language provides a vehicle for us to immerse the children in the multicultural society in which they live, developing their understanding of other cultures and languages. We strive to encourage their curiosity about other cultures and endeavour to make language learning a fun and enjoyable experience, with links across other curriculum subjects, so that our children will go on to develop further at secondary school with an enhanced awareness of their diverse world.
Cookie Policy

Music
Music
At Sunny Bank we believe that music is a vital component of the curriculum as it stimulates complex thinking which requires high levels of precision. It demands commitment and imaginative decision making. It is a powerful medium for communication between people of different ages, cultures and social backgrounds. The art of music is the aesthetic organisation of sound using the elements of rhythm, pitch, dynamics, timbre and texture, within a variety of structures. There is evidence to show that musical skills are transferable, promoting high level intellectual and physical attainment and evoking profound emotional response. Successful participation in music develops pupils’ self-esteem, well-being, confidence and learning skills. It is an effective medium for self-expression, engenders enjoyment, enhances co-operative working and promotes a sense of community.
Weekly music lessons, build upon and further develop a range of skills within this area of the curriculum.
children are encouraged to use music as a tool to express thoughts, have the freedom to reflect on experience and articulate their understanding.
We attend musical events such as London’s 02 Arena to take part in ‘Young Voices’.
Dance workshops such has Bhangra develop musical movement and expression.
Children are encouraged to participate in the school choir.
Children participate in weekly singing assemblies.
Children are given the opportunities to record their own music and create songs around real-life events.
Cookie Policy

Art
Art
At Sunny Bank, we encourage every child to experience the joy of creativity, freedom of expression, and explore their own sense of individuality. Art lessons will inspire children to think innovatively and develop creative procedural understanding. Our Art curriculum provides children with opportunities to develop their skills using a range of media and materials. Children will be introduced to a range of works and develop knowledge of the styles and vocabulary used by famous artists. The skills they acquire are applied to their cross-curricular topics, allowing children to use their art skills to reflect on and explore topics in greater depth. It is paramount that art work be purposeful; be this as a means of expression or to explore the styles of other artists that inspire our own work. Pupils should be clear what the intended outcomes are and have a means to measure their own work against this. In Art, children are expected to be reflective and evaluate their work, thinking about how they can make changes and develop their mastery of Art.
Children learn the skills of drawing, painting, printing, collage, textiles, 3D work and digital art and are given the opportunity to explore and evaluate different creative ideas.
Whole school Art exhibitions for the local community enable our children to bring their art work to life!
Art is expressed using our amazing new forest school
Children use art workshops in 3D sculpture, kite making and wood craft to further develop their skills,
‘Themed’ days create art links between a range of topics; Stone Age, Victorian and World War Two!
Cookie Policy

Computing
Computing
At Sunny Bank we recognise that our pupils are living in a rapidly changing world in which computing, IT and digital literacy are playing an ever-increasing role. The use of computers and computer systems is an integral part of the National Curriculum and knowing how they work is a key life skill. In an increasingly digital world there now exists a wealth of software, tools and technologies that can be used to communicate, collaborate, express ideas and create digital content. We recognise that pupils are entitled to a broad and balanced computing education with a structured, progressive, approach to the learning how computer systems work, the use of IT and the skills necessary to become digitally literate, further their learning and assist them in everyday life. We believe that increased IT and computing skills promote independent learning and gives greater access to a wide range of ideas and experiences
Through our computing curriculum, we ensure that our learners are digitally literate, confident and can use technology safely.
We enjoy computing through lots of practical investigations, progressing across the Key Stages.
Lessons build upon skills that are developed in the following areas; computing systems and networks, multimedia, data and information, programming and coding and online safety.
Children and teachers are encouraged to use ICT in all areas of the curriculum to further enhance learning in a range of subjects.
Cookie Policy

DT
DT
At Sunny Bank we believe that Art and Design Technology develops the child spiritually, morally, socially and culturally because we feel that children can experience a sense of awe and wonder, ask questions, consider the impact on themselves and their environment, develop life skills and encourage diversity and innovation.
Lessons are designed around a curriculum that enables our children to develop their skills in; designing and making high quality protypes, further developing their technical knowledge, understanding the principles of nutrition and learning how to cook and are given the opportunity to evaluate and test their ideas.
Lessons are creative and practical
Cross curriculum links enable our children to remember more.
Cookie Policy

Geography
Geography
At Sunny Bank we believe that Geography stimulates curiosity and imagination and geography by developing geographical skills, understanding and knowledge through studying places and themes.
We believe that Geography is a key element of the curriculum as it provides a means of exploring, appreciating and understanding the world in which we live and how it has evolved. Geography explores the relationship between the Earth and its people.
We use 6 topic-based themes across the year to ensure that children are excited and engaged through the best possible and meaningful experiences.
Our learning environment is deliberately planned to ensure that children can develop their own ideas and make links between what they know and new experiences.
Provocations and associated materials linked to the weeks story and topic are available for children to explore.
We use 3 geography based, recurring themes across the year to teach the knowledge and skills content of our geography progression maps.
Our curriculum enables the children to develop their geographical skills in; location knowledge, geographical skills and field work, human and physical geography and place knowledge.
We build in cross curricular links, where possible, so that children learn more and remember more in all subjects.
We use a range of assessment strategies throughout these lessons to ensure our children have a firm understanding of key skills and knowledge.
Cookie Policy

History
History
At Sunny Bank we aim to stimulate children’s interest and understanding about the life of people who lived in the past and ways in which it differs from the present. We believe that learning about the past helps children to make sense of the world in which they live and to develop analytical thinking.
We believe that the study of History makes a valuable contribution to the children’s understanding of all aspects of life giving a sense of identity and heritage.
We use 6 topic-based themes across the year to ensure that children are excited and engaged through the best possible and meaningful experiences.
Our learning environment is deliberately planned to ensure that children can develop their own ideas and make links between what they know and new experiences.
Provocations and associated materials linked to the weeks story and topic are available for children to explore.
We use 3 history based, recurring themes across the year to teach the knowledge and skills content of our history progression maps.
The children will develop and deepen their understanding in the following areas: chronological understanding, knowledge and understanding of events, people and changes in the past, historical interpretation and historical investigation.
Wow days and special weeks are organised to bring history to life.
We build in cross curricular links, where possible, so that children learn more and remember more in all subjects.

Sports Week launches
Sports Week launches
Semi-Pro footballer holds workshops all through the day.
To help launch our Sports Week, we had a visit today from Semi-Pro footballer Freddie Oliver. He has played for a number of clubs including Dover and Ramsgate. He now plays in the USA. pageCache.pageTitle: Sunny Bank Primary School - Late/Absence Procedures
pageCache.text:
Late/Absence Procedures
Late/Absence Procedures
The entire staff community at Sunny Bank Primary recognise the significance of
good attendance and punctuality to give the children the best chances in life.
In order to achieve high levels of attendance and punctuality we will continue to:
Offer a safe, trusting and supportive environment, which welcomes children regardless of race, gender or ability where they can flourish as individuals
Foster a climate where the school community, teachers, parents and carers, trustees and children value attendance and punctuality
Ensure any child presenting poor levels of attendance and punctuality are monitored, supported and appropriate action taken when necessary
Have systems in place offering rewards and incentives for good attendance and punctuality
Keep parents and carers informed about their child’s attendance through established procedures
Work in partnerships with parents and carers, the Education Welfare Service, Social Services, Early Help and other outside agencies
Parents and carers can help us to achieve high expectations of 100% attendance by ensuring:
Children attend regularly and on time
Children are prepared adequately for the school day
School is informed of any concerns which could impact on their child’s learning
Medical appointments are arranged outside of school hours when possible
Authorised Absence
Absence may be authorised for the following reasons:
Religious Observance in accordance with Local Authority guidelines
Medical or Dental appointments which cannot be arranged outside of school hours. Where possible parents and carers should try to arrange these appointments outside of school hours
Extenuating circumstances (authorised by the Head of School)
From the 1st September 2013, the new law gives no entitlement to parents to take their child on holiday during term time. Any application for leave must only be in exceptional circumstances and the Head of School must be satisfied that the circumstances are exceptional and warrant the granting of leave. School Leaders would not be expected to class any term time holiday as exceptional.
Unauthorised Absences
Absences may be recorded as unauthorised for the following reasons:
Late after registration is closed (unless the parent provides a legitimate reason or evidence for the absence)
Any absence which the school has not been informed about, either by letter or telephone
Any family holiday that has not been authorised by the Head of School.
Cookie Policy

pageCache.pageTitle: Sunny Bank Primary School - Staffing Changes
pageCache.text:
Staffing Changes
Staffing Changes
As we approach the end of another successful academic year, I would like to take this opportunity to inform you about several staffing changes that will be taking place at Sunny Bank Primary School.
Firstly, we will be saying goodbye to our Assistant Headteacher, Mrs Johnson, who will be leaving Sunny Bank to take up a position as Deputy Headteacher at another primary school. Mrs Johnson has been a valued member of our school community for many years and will be greatly missed by children, families and colleagues alike. As many of you know, she led the school for the majority of the 2024–2025 academic year and has played a pivotal role in many of the positive developments and improvements we have seen at Sunny Bank. We are extremely grateful for her dedication and commitment and wish her every success in her new role.
We will also be saying farewell to Mrs Hales, who has secured a promotion to the role of Assistant Headteacher at one of our Trust schools. Throughout her time at Sunny Bank, Mrs Hales has worked tirelessly to support our pupils and staff. She has led Year 6 with great success, helping pupils achieve outcomes in line with or above national averages. In addition, she has driven improvements in Literacy across the school and played an important role in supporting the development of new teachers. We congratulate her on this well-deserved promotion.
In addition, we say a fond farewell to Mrs Willing, who will be moving to another of our Trust schools, where she will take on a leadership role across Key Stage 1. Mrs Willing has made a significant contribution to Sunny Bank over the last few years, particularly through her leadership of early reading and phonics. Her work has helped many of our younger pupils make excellent progress in these essential skills. Alongside this, she has led Mathematics and Science across the school and has been instrumental in supporting our annual Science Fair entries. We thank her for all she has done and wish her every success in her new position.
Finally, we are saying goodbye to Miss Hales, who is currently on maternity leave and has made the decision not to return to Sunny Bank following the birth of her baby. We would like to thank her for her contribution to the school and send our very best wishes to her and her family for the future.
While it is always difficult to say goodbye to valued members of staff, we are delighted to be welcoming several new colleagues to Sunny Bank.
We are pleased to announce the appointment of Mrs Sukonik, an experienced Assistant Headteacher who has recently moved to Kent. Mrs Sukonik previously worked in a one-form entry primary school in London and brings a wealth of experience to our leadership team. She has already visited the school and will continue to spend time with us throughout this term as she prepares to join us formally in September.
We have also already welcomed Mrs Odumosu, an experienced Key Stage 2 teacher, to our teaching team. She is already building positive relationships with the children and making a wonderful start within our school community.
We are pleased to announce that Miss Cunningham will be remaining at Sunny Bank next year after deciding that she enjoys being part of our school community so much that she does not want to leave!
This week we have also welcomed Miss Collier, an experienced teacher from one of our other Trust schools. She is settling in well and is already getting to know the children and families.
Finally, I know that many families will be delighted to hear that Miss Shepherd will be returning to Sunny Bank in September to rejoin our teaching team.
We recognise that staffing changes can be significant for children and families. However, I am confident that these appointments will ensure we continue to build on the many strengths of our school while maintaining the high-quality education and support that our pupils deserve.
We will shortly be sharing information about class arrangements and staffing for the new academic year, so please keep an eye out for this important communication.
On behalf of everyone at Sunny Bank Primary School, I would like to thank our departing colleagues for their hard work, dedication and commitment to our children and families and to warmly welcome those who are joining us.
Cookie Policy

pageCache.pageTitle: Sunny Bank Primary School - School Reports
pageCache.text:
School Reports
School Reports
I am writing to let you know about a change to the date that our end-of-year reports are due to be sent home.
As you may be aware, there has been a national delay in the release of this year's Year 6 SATs results. As these outcomes form an important part of our reporting process, we have made the decision to postpone the distribution of all pupil reports until Monday 20th July.
We appreciate that many families look forward to receiving their child's report and understand that this change may cause some inconvenience. However, by delaying the reports, we can ensure that all reports are complete and that every family receives them at the same time, including those with children in Year 6.
Reports will therefore be sent home with pupils on Monday 20th July.
Thank you for your understanding and continued support. Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact the school office.
Cookie Policy

Enterprise Week
Enterprise Week
The children in Oak Class have been working incredibly hard to develop ideas for their fundraising activities. They have shown great creativity, teamwork and enthusiasm as they plan their enterprise projects. Throughout this week, the children will continue preparing the items they will be promoting and selling to the rest of the school tomorrow.
To enable all children to take part, we would like pupils to bring some money into school tomorrow to spend at the Year 6 Enterprise stalls. Prices range between 75p and £1.50 for fruit with chocolate, ice poles, lucky dip, penalty shoot-out, sweet cones, crisps, loom band jewellery and cakes or biscuits.
Thank you for your continued support in helping to make this exciting learning opportunity a success. We are very proud of the effort and commitment the children have shown and look forward to a fantastic Enterprise Week.
